item.title: USMCA 2026 and Economic Security: The Convergence of Technology, Trade, and National Security
item.description: CSIS Americas Program Adjunct Fellow Jake Jennings assesses pain points and areas for improved collaboration in the 2026 USMCA Joint Review.

item.title: If Compute is the New Oil, War in the Gulf Significantly Raises the Stakes
item.description: The Gulf is quickly becoming central to the global AI landscape. The United States must recognize this and adapt its partnerships accordingly.

item.title: Why Did Pakistan Announce “Open War” Against the Taliban?
item.description: Early in the morning of February 27, Pakistan’s defense minister announced “open war” between Pakistan and the Taliban, a group that Islamabad frequently backed in its 30-year quest to rule Afghanistan.

item.title: How Europe Can Build Ukraine’s Future Force
item.description: As U.S. military aid to Ukraine winds down, Europe must move beyond crisis response to lead Ukraine's long-term defense—establishing strategic coherence, hedging against U.S. disengagement, defining Ukraine's future force, and securing sustainable financing.

item.title: Northwood Declaration: The Future of European Deterrence?
item.description: The Northwood Declaration marks a major evolution in Franco British nuclear cooperation, signaling a stronger European pillar of deterrence while reinforcing NATO cohesion. Translating its ambitions into concrete policy, capability, and operational steps will shape Europe’s security future.

item.title: How Would Iran Respond to a U.S. Attack?
item.description: If the United States strikes Iran, how will Tehran respond? History suggests a calibrated mix of cyberattacks, drones, maritime pressure, and limited missile strikes designed to signal resolve while avoiding a wider regional war.

item.title: Criminal Kingpin “El Mencho” Is Dead, What Comes Next?
item.description: CSIS Americas Program Director Ryan C. Berg and Henry Ziemer analyze the implications of criminal kingpin El Mencho's death at the hands of Mexican security forces.

item.title: Industrial Policy Is Back—And Minerals Are at the Center
item.description: The United States has revived its industrial policy playbook to support critical minerals through price floors, stockpiles, and equity. But in a sector shaped by geology, cost curves, and market risk, durable security depends on commercial viability—not just public capital.
